summary: Windows exact-head regression exposed destructive lease ownership being collapsed into a reusable workflow fingerprint. The bounded repair now separates workflow/liveness identity from exact-launch ownership; final resolution still requires fresh Windows exact-head evidence.
root_cause: A reusable PID/start-token workflow fingerprint was also being used as destructive lease ownership. A distinct launch that reproduced the workflow identity could therefore be mistaken for the old owner or make takeover cleanup target the wrong ownership epoch.
repair: Preserve workflow_fingerprint for liveness compatibility, add launch_fingerprint for exact ownership, use same_launch for acquire/release/takeover ownership, treat same-workflow/different-launch as stale ownership, and preserve schema-v1 read compatibility.
resolution_condition: A fresh exact-head Windows run passes context/construction governance, supervision inspection, full product regressions including the tracked exact-launch tests, and staged consumer smoke on the final repository head.
